links.outcome: Diagnostic precision with and without a confidence threshold on LLM outputs
links.effect: Baseline accuracy 55.1%; with five-candidate list and 90% confidence threshold, precision rose to 72.9%, candidate list correct 85.9%, misdiagnosis rate 14.1%.
links.quote: By reformatting responses to list five diagnostic candidates and applying a 90% confidence threshold, the highest precision of the diagnosis increased to 72.9%, with the candidate list providing the correct diagnosis at 85.9%, reducing the misdiagnosis rate to 14.1%.

links.outcome: Trade-off between confidence-threshold deferral and number of cases answered
links.effect: The 90% confidence threshold improved precision but reduced the number of cases that received a response (no numbers given in abstract).
links.quote: However, this threshold reduced the number of cases that responded.

unlisted_practices: Prompt engineering to return a list of five diagnostic candidates

screen.reason: Empirically assesses how applying confidence thresholds and structured prompt engineering improves the diagnostic precision of an existing LLM on neuroradiology cases.
